messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a 'safety lattice' for precision selection plus an adaptive backoff policy. Runtime walks lattice nodes (FP8 -> INT8 -> 4bit) and falls back to parents when telemetry / shadow evals exceed thresholds. Wanted to surface concerns about API ergonomics, cache semantics, and required telemetry.

sam: Strong +1. Two asks: (1) make the lattice explicit in profile schema, (2) require hysteresis + configurable thresholds so we don't thrash between nodes.

leo: Runtime notes: need per-request negotiation and an `abort_on_fallback` flag so callers can opt out of silent fallback. Important: KV cache blobs are not precision-agnostic. Cache keys must include precision and profile id, e.g. `cache_key = f"{model}:{profile_id}:{precision}:{input_hash}"`. Reusing blobs across precisions will silently corrupt generations.

julia: Telemetry needs to be per-node + per-profile: emit `model_loss`, `samples`, `fallbacks`, `avg_latency_ms`, `degradation_score`. Also tag by `endpoint`, `canary_id`, and `profile_id` to slice properly.

sam: Suggest we accept an external `degradation_score` signal from shadow evaluations so policy is data-driven. Policy example: backoff when `degradation_score > X` for `Y` consecutive samples.

maria: UX question: do we expose backoff policy to customers? Proposal: a simple `safety_mode` enum exposed in SDK/console: `strict` | `managed` | `permissive`. `strict` = only run precisions explicitly pinned by profile. `managed` = runtime may use lattice and telemetry to backoff. `permissive` = allow lowest bitpaths unless customer overrides.

leo: Operations worry: too many knobs confuse users. My recommendation: ship 3 global modes + per-endpoint override metadata. Keep SDK defaults opinionated.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary `staging-nlp-12` report — fp8 shadowing since 06:30 UTC; fallback_rate=1.9% (24h), avg_latency +2.8ms, sample_count=18.

julia: Playbook suggestion: fire an alert if `fallback_rate > 1%` AND `avg_degradation_score > 0.01`. Action: auto-rollback for canaries or page SRE for production endpoints with sustained regressions.

maria: Action items: (1) schema PR to add `precision_lattice` + thresholds (assign @sam), (2) runtime changes: include precision in cache keys, add `abort_on_fallback`, persist last-successful-precision per session and add promotion TTL (assign @leo), (3) telemetry: per-node metrics + alerting (assign @julia), (4) product: finalize `safety_mode` UX and per-endpoint override. I'll open the follow-up issue and link this thread.

sam: I'll start the schema draft. Naming bikeshed: `precision_lattice` vs `quant_lattice`? Preference?

maria: Go with `precision_lattice` snake_case for clarity. Keep schema minimal to start. Example snippet for PR body (compact):

```json
{
  "precision_lattice": [
    {"node_id": "fp8_v1", "precision": "fp8", "thresholds": {"degradation_score": 0.004, "min_samples": 100}},
    {"node_id": "int8_v1", "precision": "int8", "thresholds": {"degradation_score": 0.02, "min_samples": 50}},
    {"node_id": "4bit_v1", "precision": "4bit", "thresholds": {"degradation_score": 0.06, "min_samples": 20}}
  ]
}
```

leo: Runtime caveat: backoff decisions must be idempotent. Persist last-successful-precision for a session to avoid flip-flopping, and add a cooldown TTL before allowing promotion back to lower bitwidth. Also ensure metrics emitted atomically with decisions for debugging.

maria: Sounds good — unless anyone objects I'll open the issue and tag owners. Target: land schema PR this sprint and roll telemetry to staging for a week of shadowing. Thanks all.
